title: Zita (27 April)
hookLine: a housemaid in Lucca who served one household all her working life, patron of domestic workers

lines: WORK NOTICED WHEN IT ISN'T DONE.
cards: Who cleaned the house you grew up in? Maybe a parent, after a full shift. Maybe a grandmother.
Maybe a woman who came on Thursdays and whose last name nobody in the family ever learned. Housework is the work that is noticed mainly when it isn't done. Nobody gives speeches about a clean floor.
Today's saint never ran a school, never preached, never founded anything. She scrubbed floors and baked bread for one family in the Italian city of Lucca. And the city honored her as a saint.

teach.h: A SERVANT GIRL IN ONE HOUSE.
teach.b: Zita went to work as a servant for a wealthy family in Lucca when she was still a girl, and tradition says she stayed in that house for the rest of her life. It wasn't easy at first.
The stories say the other servants resented her for working hard and praying often, and her employers treated her harshly. She kept working.

teach.h: MASS FIRST, THEN THE DAY'S WORK.
teach.b: She rose early to go to Mass, then did the day's work well. Slowly the household changed its mind about her, until she was trusted with running the house.

teach.h: BREAD FOR THE POOR, AND LEGENDS.
teach.b: She was known for giving to the poor: her own food, and sometimes, the stories admit, the family's.
One legend says her master once stopped her as she carried bread out in her apron, and when she opened it, there were only flowers.
Another says she lent her master's cloak to a freezing beggar on Christmas Eve, and a stranger brought it back. Those are legends.
The steady part isn't: a servant who worked hard, prayed, and gave.

teach.h: DO IT FROM THE HEART, AS TO THE LORD.
teach.b: Saint Paul writes to servants and masters in the letter to the Colossians, in the Douay-Rheims: "Whatsoever you do, do it from the heart, as to the Lord, and not to men." Her biographers saw Zita in that sentence.
In their telling, her work wasn't holy because it was impressive. It was holy because of whom she was doing it for. People in Lucca honored her, and the Church named her patron of domestic workers.

how: Zita is remembered on 27 April, especially in Lucca, where on her day people bring flowers to the church of San Frediano; domestic workers and those who look after homes have taken her as their patron.

games.q: you're Zita, a young servant. the other servants resent you, and your employers are harsh. what do you do?
o: keep working well, keep praying, keep giving.
games.why: the stories say she kept going, and slowly the household changed its mind until she ran the house.

practice: Bring to mind one person who cleans a space you use: the custodian at work or school, the person who cleans the hotel room, the hospital ward, the office at night.

If you don't know their name, notice that, and if the person who cleans is you, notice that too: the dishes and the laundry count. If you pray, offer your own chores, as Zita did; if you don't, just hold these people in mind.

wordCard.voice: Zita. A housemaid in Lucca who worked, prayed and gave to the poor, honored as patron of domestic workers.

carryVoice: Your line: holy in housework. A clean floor can be done as to the Lord. Until tomorrow.
